name: WPA/WPA2/WPA3 Attack Techniques
description: Ability to assess the security of WPA-family protected wireless networks. Covers four-way handshake capture and offline cracking, PMKID attacks, WPA3-SAE dragonfly handshake vulnerabilities (Dragonblood) and WPA3 transition-mode downgrade, Protected Management Frames (802.11w) enforcement, key reinstallation attacks (KRACK), fragmentation and aggregation attacks (FragAttacks), dictionary and rule-based password attacks, and assessment of pre-shared key strength. Includes understanding of countermeasures and remediation guidance.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to WPA attack techniques

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands WPA authentication mechanisms and known vulnerability classes
evidence: Can explain the WPA2 four-way handshake and its role in key derivation
Understands the difference between PSK, SAE, and Enterprise authentication
Completed training on WPA security and common attack vectors

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Executes WPA attacks against lab targets using standard tools under supervision
evidence: Captured WPA2 four-way handshakes and performed offline dictionary attacks under guidance
Executed PMKID-based attacks using hcxdumptool and hashcat under supervision
Configured and operated hash cracking rigs for WPA PSK recovery

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses WPA security and selects appropriate attack strategies
evidence: Independently assessed WPA2/WPA3 security for 3+ engagements
Selected and executed appropriate attack strategies based on target configuration
Developed engagement-specific wordlists and rule sets for targeted password attacks
Produced clear reports documenting attack methodology, results, and remediation recommendations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Executes advanced WPA attacks; assesses WPA3-SAE implementations; develops attack tooling
evidence: Assessed WPA3-SAE implementations for Dragonblood and related vulnerabilities
Performed key reinstallation (KRACK) and fragmentation/aggregation (FragAttacks) testing against client and AP implementations
Developed optimized cracking pipelines and custom wordlist generation tools
Reviews attack methodology and mentors junior staff on WPA assessment techniques

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on WPA security; discovers implementation flaws; advances lab methodology
evidence: Discovered novel implementation vulnerabilities in WPA2 or WPA3 deployments
Published research on WPA security assessment or attack techniques
Authored the lab's WPA assessment methodology and cracking infrastructure standards
Trains teams on WPA security assessment and provides vendor remediation guidance

assessment_methods.description: Assess a lab WPA2/WPA3 deployment: capture handshakes, select attack strategy, recover PSK, and document findings with remediation advice
Review reports from recent WiFi security assessments for attack methodology completeness and remediation quality

equipment: Alfa AWUS036ACH or equivalent monitor-mode-capable WiFi adapter
